- mw-cp: Mike Wright's Checkpoint Process — pre-commit checks, doc updates, detailed commit, and push
- claude-mem:do: Execute a plan using subagents for implementation
- claude-mem:make-plan: Create an implementation plan with documentation discovery
- claude-mem:mem-search: Search claude-mem's persistent cross-session memory database. Use when user asks "did we already solve this?", "how did we do X last time?", or needs work from previous sessions.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the current diff and apply the fixes — equivalent to /code-review --fix.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

21	/// Iterate every builtin name dispatched by [`call_builtin`].
22	/// Aggregates the per-module `NAMES` constants plus
23	/// [`builtins::LOCAL_NAMES`]. Used by the help-completeness
24	/// test in `mlpl-eval/tests/help_completeness_tests.rs` to
25	/// catch undocumented runtime builtins.
26	pub fn runtime_builtin_names() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static str> {
27	    builtins::LOCAL_NAMES
28	        .iter()
29	        .chain(math_builtins::NAMES)
30	        .chain(conv_builtins::NAMES)
31	        .chain(rnn_builtins::NAMES)

43	        .copied()

Components are top-level, NOT counted in sw-checklist, and are each multi-crate workspaces.

Dependency hierarchy (higher depends on lower):
- **Paths** (top) -> Tutorials -> Demos -> base

There should be a `tutorials` component and a `paths` component, each with separate crates for grouping modules per concept.

**Why:** The current monorepo has all content in one workspace. Leveled dependencies enforce that higher-level content (paths) can reference lower-level content (tutorials, demos) but not vice versa. Each component being its own workspace also helps with disk-constrained builds (separate `target/` dirs).

**How to apply:** When planning new content organization or refactoring content crates, structure as independent component workspaces with strict leveled dependencies. Don't put tutorials and paths in the same crate hierarchy as base demos.

Divide failing modules into smaller modules, move across smaller crates, move across new components. No limit on the number of components in the repo. We want small focused crates, modules, functions, and small .rs files.

Stop adding code to existing components/crates/modules unless justified. Divide built-ins into groups and spread across modules in a crate; move the crate to a new component if needed.

User-defined functions should be divided into new modules/crates in a new user-defined-function component.

**Why:** The project's sw-checklist enforces strict limits (5 fn/module, 5 module/crate) and the codebase keeps bumping those limits by accumulating code in existing files. The fix is structural: create new crates and components rather than stuffing more into existing ones.

**How to apply:** When any module/crate is at or near the limit, the default action is to create a new crate or component, NOT to add more code to the existing one. Components are top-level multi-crate workspaces not counted by sw-checklist. [[component-architecture]]

50	/// Errors produced during lexing and parsing.
51	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
52	pub enum ParseError {
53	    /// An unexpected character was encountered during lexing.
54	    UnexpectedCharacter {
55	        /// The character.
56	        ch: char,
57	        /// Where it was found.
58	        span: Span,
59	    },
60	    /// A number literal could not be parsed.
61	    InvalidNumber {
62	        /// Where the number was.
63	        span: Span,
64	    },
65	    /// An unexpected token was encountered during parsing.
66	    UnexpectedToken {
67	        /// Description of what was found.
68	        found: String,
69	        /// Where it was found.
70	        span: Span,
71	    },
72	    /// Expected a closing delimiter that was not found.
73	    UnclosedDelimiter {
74	        /// The opening delimiter.
75	        open: String,
76	        /// Where the opening delimiter was.
77	        span: Span,
78	    },

83	    },

85	    /// `{X: 1, X: 2}` errors here rather than silently picking one,
86	    /// so the eval path can assume field names are unique.
87	    DuplicateRecordField {
88	        /// The repeated field name.
89	        name: String,

91	        span: Span,
92	    },
93	}

96	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
97	        match self {
98	            Self::UnexpectedCharacter { ch, span } => {
99	                write!(f, "unexpected character '{ch}' at {span}")
100	            }
101	            Self::InvalidNumber { span } => write!(f, "invalid number at {span}"),
102	            Self::UnexpectedToken { found, span } => {
103	                write!(f, "unexpected token '{found}' at {span}")
104	            }
105	            Self::UnclosedDelimiter { open, span } => {

107	            }
108	            Self::InvalidUtf8 { span } => {
109	                write!(f, "invalid UTF-8 in string literal at {span}")
110	            }
111	            Self::DuplicateRecordField { name, span } => {
112	                write!(f, "duplicate record field '{name}' at {span}")
113	            }
114	        }
115	    }
116	}

1	//! Token types for the MLPL lexer.
2	
3	use mlpl_core::Span;
4	
5	/// The kind of a lexer token.
6	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
7	pub enum TokenKind {
8	    /// Integer literal.
9	    IntLit(i64),
10	    /// Float literal.
11	    FloatLit(f64),
12	    /// Identifier.
13	    Ident(String),
14	    /// Builtin / operator reference: `:foo`, `:+`, `:max`, `:*`.
15	    /// The lexer produces this whenever a `:` is immediately
16	    /// followed (no intervening space) by an identifier-start
17	    /// character or one of `+ * / -`. The annotation colon
18	    /// (`x : [batch] = ...`) keeps producing `Colon` because
19	    /// it requires a space after the `:`, then a `[`. This
20	    /// is the canonical way to pass a function / operator
21	    /// reference to a higher-order builtin like `reduce` or
22	    /// `map`. See `docs/glossary.md` "Reduce".
23	    BuiltinRef(String),
24	    /// String literal (double-quoted, escapes processed).
25	    StrLit(String),
26	    /// `(`
27	    LParen,
28	    /// `)`
29	    RParen,
30	    /// `[`
31	    LBracket,
32	    /// `]`
33	    RBracket,
34	    /// `,`
35	    Comma,
36	    /// `=`
37	    Equals,
38	    /// `:` (axis-label annotation, Saga 11.5 Phase 2).
39	    Colon,
40	    /// `;`
41	    Semicolon,
42	    /// `+`
43	    Plus,
44	    /// `-`
45	    Minus,
46	    /// `*`
47	    Star,
48	    /// `/`
49	    Slash,
50	    /// `{`
51	    LBrace,
52	    /// `}`
53	    RBrace,
54	    /// `.` (field access on records, Saga 29 step 001). Distinct
55	    /// from float-literal decimal points -- floats lex via
56	    /// `lex_number` which only consumes `digit.digit`; a bare `.`
57	    /// at the lexer fall-through is this token.
58	    Dot,
59	    /// `repeat` keyword.
60	    Repeat,
61	    /// `train` keyword.
62	    Train,
63	    /// `for` keyword (streaming-iter, Saga 12 step 003).
64	    For,
65	    /// `in` keyword (only meaningful inside `for ... in ...`).
66	    In,
67	    /// `experiment` keyword (Saga 12 step 007).
68	    Experiment,
69	    /// `device` keyword (Saga 14 step 004). Introduces a scoped
70	    /// `device("mlx") { body }` or `device("cpu") { body }` block
71	    /// that dispatches ops inside the body through the named
72	    /// runtime target.
73	    Device,
74	    /// `if` keyword (Saga 31 step 004). Introduces an `if cond
75	    /// { then } else { else }` expression that returns the value
76	    /// of whichever branch was taken. `else` is required.
77	    If,
78	    /// `else` keyword (Saga 31 step 004). Always paired with `if`.
79	    Else,
80	    /// `while` keyword (Saga 31 step 005). Introduces a `while cond
81	    /// { body }` loop. Exits when `cond` is falsy or `break` fires.
82	    While,
83	    /// `break` keyword (Saga 31 step 005). Exits the nearest
84	    /// enclosing `while` loop. Optionally followed by a value.
85	    Break,
86	    /// `continue` keyword (Saga 31 step 005). Skips the rest of
87	    /// the current `while` iteration; cond is re-checked.
88	    Continue,
89	    /// `def` keyword (Saga 46). Introduces a user-defined function.
90	    Def,
91	    /// `return` keyword (Saga 46). Early exit from a UDF body.
92	    Return,
93	    /// Newline (statement separator).
94	    Newline,
95	    /// End of input.
96	    Eof,
97	}
98	
99	/// A token with its source span.
100	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
101	pub struct Token {
102	    /// What kind of token.
103	    pub kind: TokenKind,
104	    /// Where in the source.
105	    pub span: Span,
106	}

content.content:
Insert a new pending step at a chosen position, shifting later steps up

Use when a bug or unplanned task needs to slot in before existing pending work. The new step lands at position `after + 1`; every pending/in-progress step with a number greater than `after` shifts up by one (step.toml `number` and the on-disk `NNN-slug` directory name are both updated). The operation is refused if any step that would shift is already `Completed`, since completed steps anchor git-tracked history.

Pass `--after 0` to prepend at position 1 (only works if step 1 is pending).

Cursor semantic (preemption): if the new step lands at or before the current cursor, focus follows the new arrival — the inserted step becomes `current_step` and the previously focused step is pushed to `current_step + 1`. This matches the "drop in a blocker" use case. If the new step lands behind the cursor, focus is unchanged and the new step is queued as future work.

use mlpl_array::DenseArray;
use mlpl_runtime_core::error::RuntimeError;

pub const NAMES: &[&str] = &[
    "iota",
    "range",
    "shape",
    "rank",
    "reshape",
    "transpose",
    "reduce_add",
    "reduce_mul",
    "argmax",
    "dot",
    "matmul",
    "patchify",
    "take",
];
// Note: `concat` is dispatched through builtins.rs match (3-arg form)
// and mlpl-runtime-math NAMES (2-arg legacy form). Not listed here so
// runtime_builtin_names doesn't duplicate it.

pub fn try_call(name: &str, args: Vec<DenseArray>) -> Option<Result<DenseArray, RuntimeError>> {
    match name {
        "iota" | "range" => Some(crate::compute::iota(name, args)),
        "shape" => Some(crate::shape::shape(name, args)),
        "rank" => Some(crate::shape::rank(name, args)),
        "reshape" => Some(crate::shape::reshape(name, args)),
        "transpose" => Some(crate::shape::transpose(name, args)),
        "reduce_add" | "reduce_mul" => Some(crate::reduce::reduce(name, args)),
        "argmax" => Some(crate::reduce::argmax(name, args)),
        "dot" => Some(crate::compute::dot(name, args)),
        "matmul" => Some(crate::compute::matmul(name, args)),
        "patchify" => Some(crate::slice::patchify(name, args)),
        "concat" if args.len() == 3 => Some(crate::slice::concat(name, args)),
        "take" => Some(crate::slice::take(name, args)),
        _ => None,
    }
}

use mlpl_array::DenseArray;
use mlpl_runtime_core::error::RuntimeError;

pub const NAMES: &[&str] = &[
    "iota",
    "range",
    "shape",
    "rank",
    "reshape",
    "transpose",
    "reduce_add",
    "reduce_mul",
    "argmax",
    "dot",
    "matmul",
    "patchify",
    "take",
];
// Note: `concat` is dispatched through builtins.rs match (3-arg form)
// and mlpl-runtime-math NAMES (2-arg legacy form). Not listed here so
// runtime_builtin_names doesn't duplicate it.

pub fn try_call(name: &str, args: Vec<DenseArray>) -> Option<Result<DenseArray, RuntimeError>> {
    match name {
        "iota" | "range" => Some(crate::compute::iota(name, args)),
        "shape" => Some(crate::shape::shape(name, args)),
        "rank" => Some(crate::shape::rank(name, args)),
        "reshape" => Some(crate::shape::reshape(name, args)),
        "transpose" => Some(crate::shape::transpose(name, args)),
        "reduce_add" | "reduce_mul" => Some(crate::reduce::reduce(name, args)),
        "argmax" => Some(crate::reduce::argmax(name, args)),
        "dot" => Some(crate::compute::dot(name, args)),
        "matmul" => Some(crate::compute::matmul(name, args)),
        "patchify" => Some(crate::slice::patchify(name, args)),
        "concat" if args.len() == 3 => Some(crate::slice::concat(name, args)),
        "take" => Some(crate::slice::take(name, args)),
        _ => None,
    }
}

content.text:
Good question. Let me address the strategy and then start the extraction.

## Strategy Analysis: Where to attack first?

**Worst-offenders first wins.** Here's why:

**Top (components):** Currently only 1 component exists (`mlpl-session`). Components are unbounded — no FAILs at this level. Working here is pure infrastructure setup with delayed payoff.

**Middle (crates with too many modules):** This is where the worst offenders live:
- `mlpl-eval` (96 modules, 14× over budget)
- `mlpl-web` (75 modules, 11× over budget)
- `mlpl-array` (13 modules), `mlpl-viz` (13 modules)

**Bottom (modules with too many fns):** Often blocked by middle. Can't split a module if the crate is already at module-count FAIL — you'd just trade one FAIL for another.

**The dependency chain:** splitting a function needs module room → splitting a module needs crate room → splitting a crate needs component room. When `mlpl-eval` has 96 modules (FAIL), any internal cleanup is wasted motion until the crate is decomposed.

**Right order:**
1. **Worst middle offenders first** (mlpl-eval, mlpl-web) — they're so far over budget that they block everything downstream and consume warning budgets unfairly.
2. **In parallel: continue extracting from at-capacity crates** like mlpl-runtime (where we have proven patterns).
3. **Components only when** a logical grouping spans crates that should level (e.g., paths > tutorials > demos).
4. **Bottom-up cleanup last** — after the structural FAILs are gone.

What I've been doing on mlpl-runtime is the right pattern *for that crate*. But the leverage point for the whole codebase is **mlpl-eval and mlpl-web**.

Now let me set up step 004 and extract mlpl-runtime-ml.

1	//! Built-in function registry and dispatch.
2	//!
3	//! Most array/shape/reduce/slice builtins live in
4	//! `mlpl-runtime-array`; the rest are dispatched through the
5	//! `try_external_dispatchers` chain below. This module only
6	//! holds the dispatch glue plus the `grid` / `concat` (2-arg)
7	//! arms that don't fit the per-crate `try_call` pattern.
8	
9	use mlpl_array::DenseArray;
10	
11	use mlpl_runtime_core::error::RuntimeError;
12	
13	/// Names handled by the local match in `match_local_builtin`
14	/// below (i.e., names NOT covered by any per-crate `try_call`).
15	/// Currently just `grid`, which dispatches into mlpl-runtime-data.
16	pub(crate) const LOCAL_NAMES: &[&str] = &["grid"];
17	
18	/// Try every external per-module `try_call` dispatcher in
19	/// registration order; returns `Some(result)` for the first
20	/// module that recognizes `name`.
21	fn try_external_dispatchers(
22	    name: &str,
23	    args: &[DenseArray],
24	) -> Option<Result<DenseArray, RuntimeError>> {
25	    mlpl_runtime_math::try_call(name, args.to_vec())
26	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_array::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
27	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_conv::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
28	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_rnn::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
29	        .or_else(|| crate::random_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
30	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_data::dataset_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
31	        .or_else(|| crate::ml_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
32	        .or_else(|| crate::ensemble_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
33	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_data::embedding_builtins::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
34	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_dim_reduction::tsne_builtin::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
35	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_dim_reduction::pca_builtin::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
36	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_umap::umap_graph::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
37	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_umap::umap_builtin::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
38	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_mds_rp::mds::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
39	        .or_else(|| mlpl_runtime_mds_rp::random_projection::try_call(name, args.to_vec()))
40	}
41	
42	/// Dispatch a built-in function call by name.
43	pub fn call_builtin(name: &str, args: Vec<DenseArray>) -> Result<DenseArray, RuntimeError> {
44	    if let Some(result) = try_external_dispatchers(name, &args) {
45	        return result;
46	    }
47	    match_local_builtin(name, args)
48	}
49	
50	/// Match the local in-crate builtin names. Currently just `grid`
51	/// (which lives in mlpl-runtime-data but isn't behind a `try_call`).
52	fn match_local_builtin(name: &str, args: Vec<DenseArray>) -> Result<DenseArray, RuntimeError> {
53	    match name {
54	        "grid" => mlpl_runtime_data::grid_builtin::builtin_grid(name, args),
55	        _ => Err(RuntimeError::UnknownFunction(name.into())),
56	    }
57	}

metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When extracting a logical group of crates, put them in a **component** (a top-level multi-crate workspace under `components/<name>/`), NOT flat in the main `sw-mlpl/crates/` directory.

**Each major feature should be its own component.** Many, many components. Each component has a few sparse crates; each crate has a few sparse modules; each module has a few sparse functions.

**Why:** The user has repeatedly emphasized this. Flat workspace = sprawl that fights the sw-checklist limits. Components are unbounded (not counted by sw-checklist) and provide natural decomposition boundaries. The existing `components/mlpl-session/` is the model.

**How to apply:**
- Before extracting a new crate, ask: which component does this belong in?
- If the natural component doesn't exist yet, **create it** as part of the extraction
- Don't just dump new crates into `sw-mlpl/crates/` — that's the failure mode
- When refactoring, look for groups of related crates already in `crates/` and migrate them into a new component together

**Concrete groupings to create:**
- `components/mlpl-runtime/` — runtime + all runtime-* crates (math, conv, rnn, array, ml, data, dim-reduction, umap, mds-rp, core)
- `components/mlpl-language/` — core, array, parser, lexer, macro
- `components/mlpl-eval/` — eval, eval-core, web-eval, autograd
- `components/mlpl-web/` — web app + web-lessons + web-path-body + viz
- `components/mlpl-tools/` — repl, cli, build, lab, serve, reg
- `components/mlpl-models/` — already exists as mlpl-session, expand

## What I did wrong, and the proposed fix

**What I did wrong:** I extracted 6 new crates this session but landed all of them flat in `sw-mlpl/crates/` — the exact sprawl pattern you've told me to avoid. I treated `components/mlpl-session/` as an outlier rather than the model to follow.

**The fix — proposed component structure:**

```
sw-mlpl/
├── components/
│   ├── mlpl-runtime/           # runtime + math + conv + rnn + array + ml + data + dim-reduction + umap + mds-rp + core
│   ├── mlpl-language/          # core + array + lexer + parser + macro + lower-rs
│   ├── mlpl-eval/              # eval + eval-core + autograd + ml
│   ├── mlpl-web/               # mlpl-web app + web-eval + web-lessons + web-path-body + viz + wasm

│   ├── mlpl-trace/             # trace + rt + mlx-rt
│   └── mlpl-session/           # (already exists) models
└── crates/                     # (eventually empty or minimal)
```

**This is a HARD RULE, not a preference.** The user has flagged this across many sessions and many commits.

NEVER create a new crate flat in `sw-mlpl/crates/`. Every new crate goes into a `components/<feature>/crates/` workspace.

If the right component doesn't exist yet, **create the component as part of the extraction.** The existing `components/mlpl-session/` is the model — a nested workspace with its own `Cargo.toml` and its own `crates/` subdirectory.

**Why:** Components are top-level multi-crate workspaces, not counted by sw-checklist. Flat `crates/` is sprawl that fights the limits. The user has repeatedly emphasized: many components, each sparse with a few crates, each crate sparse with a few modules, each module sparse with a few functions. This is the project's architectural intent.

**How to apply — DO THIS BEFORE EXTRACTING ANYTHING:**
1. Identify the feature/concern of the code being extracted
2. Check if `components/<that-feature>/` exists. If not, plan to create it
3. Add the new crate UNDER `components/<feature>/crates/<crate-name>/`, NOT in `sw-mlpl/crates/<crate-name>/`
4. The component's `Cargo.toml` is the nested workspace manifest
5. The main `sw-mlpl/Cargo.toml` should NOT list crates that live inside a component
6. Use a single shared `target/` via `.cargo/config.toml` at the repo root with `[build] target-dir = "target"` to avoid per-component target dirs

**If a feature has only one crate today,** it still goes into a component — the component will accumulate sibling crates over time as the feature gains structure.

**Detection check before every `cargo new` / `mkdir crates/...`:** ask "which component does this live in?" If the answer is "the main workspace", that's wrong — stop, find or create the right component.

content.text:
Now the plan you asked for. Below is a complete physical layout based on the dependency data I just collected.

---

# Component Restructuring Plan

## Principles

1. **Components are top-level features.** Each represents one cohesive concern of the system.
2. **Components contain sparse crates** (few crates per component); crates contain sparse modules; modules contain sparse functions.
3. **Dependencies flow downward only** — strict DAG; no cycles between components.
4. **Shared `target/`** via `.cargo/config.toml` at the repo root.
5. **No crate lives directly in `sw-mlpl/crates/`** — that directory becomes empty (or deleted) after migration.

## Dependency layers (bottom → top)

From the data I collected:

```
Layer 0 (no intra-workspace deps): mlpl-core, mlpl-eval-core, mlpl-bpe-core,
                                   mlpl-web-lessons, mlpl-web-path-body, mlpl-lab

Layer 1 (depend on Layer 0):       mlpl-array, mlpl-lexer

Layer 2:                           mlpl-parser, mlpl-loader-helpers,
                                   mlpl-runtime-core, mlpl-trace, mlpl-rt,
                                   mlpl-autograd

Layer 3:                           mlpl-runtime-{math,conv,rnn,array,ml,data,
                                                 dim-reduction,umap,mds-rp},
                                   mlpl-mlx-rt, mlpl-viz, mlpl-lower-rs,
                                   mlpl-env-traits

Layer 4:                           mlpl-runtime, mlpl-macro, mlpl-models-*,
                                   mlpl-ml

Layer 5:                           mlpl-eval, mlpl-wasm

Layer 6:                           mlpl-cli, mlpl-bench, mlpl-parity-tests,
                                   mlpl-reg, mlpl-web-eval

Layer 7:                           mlpl-serve, mlpl-build, mlpl

Layer 8 (apps):                    mlpl-repl, mlpl-web, mlpl-mlx-serve
```

## Proposed components

### `components/lang-core/` — language foundations
**Purpose:** Types and primitives every other component depends on. Pure data, no behavior.

| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-core` | spans, identifiers, base types |
| `mlpl-array` | DenseArray, Shape (pure compute substrate) |
| `mlpl-eval-core` | shared eval types (no eval logic) |

**Why grouped:** all Layer 0–1, depended on by every other component. The foundation.

---

### `components/lang-syntax/` — lexer + parser + AST
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-lexer` | tokens, lexing |
| `mlpl-parser` | AST + parser |
| `mlpl-macro` | proc macros |
| `mlpl-lower-rs` | parser → IR lowering |

**Why grouped:** the source-text-to-AST pipeline. All sit between core and any consumer that reads MLPL source.

**Depends on:** `lang-core`

---

### `components/runtime/` — built-in function runtime
| Crate | Role |
|-------|------|
| `mlpl-runtime-core` | RuntimeError, prng |
| `mlpl-runtime-math` | math + constructor builtins |
| `mlpl-runtime-array` | shape/reduce/slice/linalg builtins |
| `mlpl-runtime-conv` | conv2d, pool2d |
| `mlpl-runtime-rnn` | rnn_cell, lstm_cell |

## Component dependency graph (DAG)

```
lang-core ─────────────────────────┐
   ↓                                ↓
lang-syntax                    runtime
   ↓ ↓                              ↓
   ↓ ↓     autograd ←───────────────┘
   ↓ ↓        ↓
   ↓ ↓        ↓     native-rt ←── lang-core
   ↓ ↓        ↓        ↓
   ↓ ↓        ↓     viz ← autograd
   ↓ ↓        ↓        ↓
   ↓ ↓       models ←──┘
   ↓ ↓        ↓
   eval ←─────┘
     ↓
   ┌─┴─┬─────────┬─────────┐
   ↓   ↓         ↓         ↓
 wasm  cli    serve     dev-tools
   ↓
  web
```

No cycles. Every component depends only on lower layers.

## Shared `target/` setup

Create `sw-mlpl/.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[build]
target-dir = "target"
```

Cargo discovers `.cargo/config.toml` by walking up from the current directory. Any `cargo` invocation from anywhere in the tree resolves the same shared `target/` at `sw-mlpl/target/`. No per-component target dirs. Disk-friendly.

## Migration plan (12 steps, one saga each)

Order matters — bottom-up so dependents always compile.

| Step | Component | Crates moved | Rationale |
|------|-----------|--------------|-----------|
| 1 | Set up `.cargo/config.toml` shared target | — | enable rest of plan |
| 2 | `lang-core` | mlpl-core, mlpl-array, mlpl-eval-core | foundation; everything depends on it |
| 3 | `lang-syntax` | mlpl-lexer, mlpl-parser, mlpl-macro, mlpl-lower-rs | next layer up |
| 4 | `runtime` | 11 runtime-* crates | clean self-contained family |
| 5 | `autograd` | mlpl-autograd, mlpl-trace | small, independent |
| 6 | `native-rt` | mlpl-rt, mlpl-mlx-rt | small, independent |
| 7 | `viz` | mlpl-viz | single-crate component |
| 8 | Rename `mlpl-session` → `models` | — | cosmetic, optional, ask first |
| 9 | `eval` | mlpl-eval | single-crate now; future decomposition next saga |
| 10 | `wasm` | mlpl-wasm, mlpl-web-eval | depends on eval |
| 11 | `cli` + `serve` | apps + mlpl-cli + mlpl-serve + mlpl-mlx-serve, mlpl, mlpl-build, mlpl-lab, mlpl-repl | top of stack |
| 12 | `web` + `dev-tools` | mlpl-web, web-lessons, web-path-body, bench, parity-tests, reg | leaf consumers |

Each step: create component, move crates with `git mv`, update path deps inside moved crates, remove from root `Cargo.toml`, verify `cargo check` from a clean state.

## Per-step recipe

1. `mkdir -p components/<name>/crates`
2. Write `components/<name>/Cargo.toml` workspace manifest
3. `git mv` each crate from `crates/<x>/` to `components/<name>/crates/<x>/`
4. Update path dependencies in moved crates: `path = "../../<other-component>/crates/<dep>"` for cross-component deps; `path = "../<dep>"` for same-component
5. Remove moved crates from root `Cargo.toml` members
6. `cargo check --workspace` (from each affected workspace root)
7. `cargo test` for affected crates
8. Commit; push

1. **Rename `mlpl-session` → `models`?** Cosmetic but consistent. (Default: leave as-is to minimize churn.)
2. **Apps in components/cli/ and components/web/, or keep `apps/`?** I'd fold them in for consistency. Confirm.
3. **Order — start with bottom (`lang-core`) or the just-extracted `runtime` family that's freshest in my head?** I lean bottom-up but happy either way.
4. **One saga = one component, or batch multiple into one?** I'd do one saga per component for safety; you've taught me to keep diffs reviewable.

Tell me which questions to resolve and I'll start with whichever component you want first.

workspaces (main + each component) write to the same build cache.

migration. It lives by itself in saga 51 so the migration sagas
(saga 52 onward, one per component) start from a clean baseline.

# Single shared target directory for the whole repo.
#
# Cargo discovers this config by walking up from the invocation
# directory. Any `cargo` command -- whether run from this main
# workspace, from a nested component workspace under components/,
# or from a service under services/ -- resolves to the same
# target/ tree at the repo root.
#
# Why: as the project decomposes into many component workspaces
# (saga 51+), each would otherwise grow its own multi-GB target/.
# A single shared target keeps disk usage bounded (~25 GB after a
# full build vs N x 25 GB) and makes cross-workspace incremental
# rebuilds cache-warm.
#
# `target-dir` is relative to this config file's directory, so it
# resolves to sw-mlpl/target/ regardless of where cargo is invoked
# from.

[build]
target-dir = "target"

# components/lang-core/ migration (saga 52)

First component-migration saga. Move the three foundational crates
(mlpl-core, mlpl-array, mlpl-eval-core) into a new
`components/lang-core/` nested workspace. Bottom of the dep stack,
so every other crate's path references must be updated.

## Why these three together

- mlpl-core: spans, identifiers, base types -- depended on by ~15
- mlpl-array: DenseArray, Shape -- depended on by ~30
- mlpl-eval-core: shared eval types -- depended on by ~7

All Layer 0-1, no intra-workspace deps among them except
mlpl-array -> mlpl-core. Move them together so referrers update
once, not three times.

## Step plan

1. **scaffold-component**: create `components/lang-core/Cargo.toml`
   (workspace manifest), `components/lang-core/crates/` empty
   directory. Verify the empty component workspace builds.
2. **move-mlpl-core**: `git mv crates/mlpl-core
   components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-core`. Update root Cargo.toml
   members. Update every Cargo.toml that has
   `mlpl-core = { path = "../mlpl-core" }` to point to the new
   location. Verify full workspace build.
3. **move-mlpl-array**: `git mv` then update all referrers (the
   biggest batch -- ~30 crates).
4. **move-mlpl-eval-core**: `git mv` then update all referrers
   (~7 crates).
5. **close**: language-status update, --done.

Each step ends with a green `cargo check --workspace` and pushed
commits, so no step leaves the tree broken.

## Path-reference rules

Crates currently in `crates/<foo>/` referring to a moved crate:
`mlpl-core = { path = "../../components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-core" }`

Crates in `components/<other>/crates/<foo>/` referring to a moved
crate: `mlpl-core = { path = "../../../lang-core/crates/mlpl-core" }`

Crates in `apps/<foo>/` referring to a moved crate:
`mlpl-core = { path = "../../components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-core" }`

Crates in `services/<foo>/` referring to a moved crate:
`mlpl-core = { path = "../../components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-core" }`

## Shared target

Already in place from saga 51. The new component workspace inherits
.cargo/config.toml automatically and writes to the same target/.
EOF

---
name: no-git-add-all
description: Never use `git add -A` or `git add .` — always stage specific files; bulk-staging sweeps in untracked scratch
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Never use `git add -A` or `git add .` in this repo. Always stage specific files by name or directory.

**Why:** The repo's working tree often has untracked files that should NOT be committed:
- `tmp/` — scratch drafts and prereq prompts
- `.DS_Store` — macOS Finder metadata
- `docs/*.jpg`/draft markdown — works in progress

A bulk-stage sweeps these in and pollutes history. I made this mistake during saga 52 step 002 — `git add -A` swept in tmp/ and .DS_Store. Required a follow-up cleanup commit.

**How to apply:**
- Stage by explicit paths: `git add components/lang-core/ crates/mlpl-array/Cargo.toml ...`
- Use `git add -u` for "stage modifications to already-tracked files" — that's safe; it doesn't add new untracked files
- For mixed additions, list each new file explicitly
- After staging, ALWAYS run `git status --short` and re-check there's nothing you didn't intend

# Saga 52: components/lang-core/ nested workspace.
#
# Houses the foundational data types that every other component
# depends on:
#   - mlpl-core: spans, identifiers, base types
#   - mlpl-array: DenseArray, Shape (pure compute substrate)
#   - mlpl-eval-core: shared eval types
#
# Pattern matches components/mlpl-session/: a nested workspace
# whose member crates are removed from the main workspace's
# members list. Path deps reach across components via relative
# paths like `../../../<other-component>/crates/<dep>`.
#
# Build cache is shared via `.cargo/config.toml` at the repo root
# (saga 51), so this workspace writes to `sw-mlpl/target/` not
# its own target subdirectory.

[workspace]
members = [
    "crates/mlpl-array",
    "crates/mlpl-core",
]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
edition = "2024"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
version = "0.20.0"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"

You're absolutely right — the whole point. A move is just relocation. The retirement comes from splitting the crowded crate into sparse siblings within the component. mlpl-array has 13 modules (FAIL); leaving it as one crate inside lang-core doesn't retire anything. Splitting it into `mlpl-array-dense` / `mlpl-array-shape` / `mlpl-array-indexing` / `mlpl-array-ops` (each sparse) retires the FAIL and gives the component its purpose.

input.content:
---
name: move-and-split
description: A component migration is move-and-split — moving without splitting crowded crates leaves the FAILs intact and misses the whole point
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A component migration is **move-AND-split**, not just move.

When you move a crowded crate (one with module-count or fn-count FAILs/WARNs) into a new component, the same saga must also SPLIT it into multiple sparse sibling crates within that component. Otherwise the FAIL persists in the moved crate and the migration achieved nothing structural — just relocation.

**Why:** The whole point of having components is that components hold *sparse* sibling crates. A component containing one 13-module crate is no better than the original flat workspace had — sw-checklist still FAILs on that crate. The retirements come from the split: 1 crate with 13 modules (FAIL) → 4 sibling crates with 3-4 modules each (PASS).

**How to apply:**
- Before each component migration saga, identify which crates inside the target component are crowded (>7 modules, >7 fns/module, or any FAIL)
- The saga's step plan must include `split-<crate>` steps for each crowded crate, not just `move-<crate>` steps
- The close step's sw-checklist delta SHOULD show retired FAILs after a component migration — if it shows zero delta, the migration was incomplete
- Example: lang-core's saga (52) closed with 0 FAILs retired despite moving mlpl-array (13 modules, FAIL). That was wrong — the saga should have included a `split-mlpl-array` step that decomposed it into siblings.

**Concrete crowded crates to split during their migration saga:**
- mlpl-array: 13 modules -> split during lang-core saga (need to revisit saga 52 OR do a follow-up saga)
- mlpl-viz: 13 modules -> split during viz saga
- mlpl-eval: 96 modules -> split into many siblings during eval saga (catastrophic; needs careful sub-planning)
- mlpl-web: 75 modules -> split into many siblings during web saga
- mlpl-serve: 9 modules -> split during serve saga
- mlpl-runtime: 4 modules (PASS), but builtins.rs may still need attention
- mlpl-autograd: 7 modules at the limit + 2 modules with FAIL fn-counts (backward, reduction_ops)

When you move a crowded crate (one with module-count or fn-count FAILs/WARNs) into a new component, the same saga must also SPLIT it into multiple sparse sibling crates within that component. Otherwise the FAIL persists in the moved crate and the migration achieved nothing structural — just relocation.

**Why:** The whole point of having components is that components hold *sparse* sibling crates. A component containing one 13-module crate is no better than the original flat workspace had — sw-checklist still FAILs on that crate. The retirements come from the split: 1 crate with 13 modules (FAIL) → 4 sibling crates with 3-4 modules each (PASS).

**How to apply:**
- Before each component migration saga, identify which crates inside the target component are crowded (>7 modules, >7 fns/module, or any FAIL)
- The saga's step plan must include `split-<crate>` steps for each crowded crate, not just `move-<crate>` steps
- The close step's sw-checklist delta SHOULD show retired FAILs after a component migration — if it shows zero delta, the migration was incomplete
- Example: lang-core's saga (52) closed with 0 FAILs retired despite moving mlpl-array (13 modules, FAIL). That was wrong — the saga should have included a `split-mlpl-array` step that decomposed it into siblings.

**Concrete crowded crates to split during their migration saga:**
- mlpl-array: 13 modules -> split during lang-core saga (need to revisit saga 52 OR do a follow-up saga)
- mlpl-viz: 13 modules -> split during viz saga
- mlpl-eval: 96 modules -> split into many siblings during eval saga (catastrophic; needs careful sub-planning)
- mlpl-web: 75 modules -> split into many siblings during web saga
- mlpl-serve: 9 modules -> split during serve saga
- mlpl-runtime: 4 modules (PASS), but builtins.rs may still need attention
- mlpl-autograd: 7 modules at the limit + 2 modules with FAIL fn-counts (backward, reduction_ops)

# Saga 52: components/lang-core/ nested workspace.
#
# Houses the foundational data types that every other component
# depends on:
#   - mlpl-core: spans, identifiers, base types
#   - mlpl-array: DenseArray, Shape (pure compute substrate)
#   - mlpl-eval-core: shared eval types
#
# Pattern matches components/mlpl-session/: a nested workspace
# whose member crates are removed from the main workspace's
# members list. Path deps reach across components via relative
# paths like `../../../<other-component>/crates/<dep>`.
#
# Build cache is shared via `.cargo/config.toml` at the repo root
# (saga 51), so this workspace writes to `sw-mlpl/target/` not
# its own target subdirectory.

[workspace]
members = [
    "crates/mlpl-array",
    "crates/mlpl-core",
    "crates/mlpl-eval-core",
]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
edition = "2024"
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
version = "0.20.0"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
pedantic = "warn"

---
name: test-refactors
description: Every refactor step must run `cargo test` on the affected crates to verify behavior is preserved, not just `cargo check`
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Every refactor step must verify there are no regressions, not just that the code still compiles. `cargo check` proves the type system is happy; `cargo test` proves behavior is preserved.

**Why:** The user has been burned by refactors that "compile clean" but silently broke runtime behavior — golden outputs change, demos misbehave, integration tests fail. A move/split that passes `cargo check` is only halfway done.

**How to apply per refactor step:**
1. `cargo check --workspace` AND each component's `cargo check` from its root — type-level safety
2. `cargo test -p <affected-crate>` for every crate touched — direct unit/integration tests
3. `cargo test -p <downstream-crate>` for at least one or two downstream consumers — catch breakages where the refactor changed an interface
4. For interpreter or eval changes: `cargo test -p mlpl-eval --release` to verify demos still work
5. If any test fails, fix it before committing — don't ship a broken refactor

**Specific places this matters:**
- Moving a function from inherent impl to extension trait — semantic equivalence depends on resolution order; test the exact call sites
- Splitting a crate — tests in the original crate that test moved functionality should still work (use dev-deps to import the new sibling)
- Renaming/restructuring — golden-file tests catch what unit tests miss

[[no-blind-golden-rebase]]

add_dep() {
  local file=$1
  local rel=$2
  if ! grep -q 'mlpl-array-ops-reduce = ' "$file"; then
    awk -v rel="$rel" '
      /^mlpl-array = / && !done { print; print "mlpl-array-ops-reduce = { path = \"" rel "\" }"; done=1; next }
      { print }
    ' "$file" > "$file.new" && mv "$file.new" "$file"
  fi
}

cat >> components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array/Cargo.toml <<'EOF'

add_dep crates/mlpl-runtime-array/Cargo.toml "../../components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array-ops-reduce"

  components/lang-core/crates/mlpl-array/tests/dense_tests.rs \

done

add_dep() {
  local file=$1
  local rel=$2
  if ! grep -q 'mlpl-array-ops-compose = ' "$file"; then
    awk -v rel="$rel" '
      /^mlpl-array = / && !done { print; print "mlpl-array-ops-compose = { path = \"" rel "\" }"; done=1; next }
      { print }
    ' "$file" > "$file.new" && mv "$file.new" "$file"
  fi
}
